title: Save 47,523 instructions in the 512-point NTT multiplier (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Save exactly **47,523 executed instructions on every admitted input** to the 512-point bounded Word RAM multiplier. Static length falls by 72,051 instructions:

```diff
-static instructions: 507,701
+static instructions: 435,650
```

Claim type: scoped program-refinement proof with a source-bound finite certificate, produced by Nick Petalas. Each of 1,533 constant-one transform-twiddle macros becomes two literal instructions preserving complete memory, including the scratch temporary. For transform size n, the exact static and executed savings are 141(n-1) and 93(n-1). The proof is a block simulation with explicit branch relocation; finite checks corroborate it.

David Ganz / Dugongue’s PR #5466 supplies the original multiplier, ISA, NTT schedule, residue invariants and all-input multiplication theorem as cited premises. This contribution builds a new arithmetic refinement; it does not audit that theorem. Its retained tcslib, FastPoly, CatCrypt, mpfx and predecessor notices keep their credit. Constant specialization and block simulation are standard methods; no literature-wide priority claim is made.

Only `research/wordram-unit-twiddles/` is added. Frozen sources and the selected frontier are unchanged. The formal-interface-lemma card is explicitly changed to this bounded compiler/cost side result; no formalization or selected framework assumption is discharged. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19441308).

## Evidence

- **Before:** a unit twiddle executes the generic 49-instruction modular-product macro in exactly 33 instructions. **After:** two instructions produce identical VALUE, TEMP and exterior memory, saving exactly 47 static and 31 executed instructions per site.
- All 65,537 local residues pass complete-memory equivalence, with dirty scratch and exterior fixtures. The verifier enumerates all replacement sites in nine balanced templates through 512 points; 36 complete dirty-memory executions check the new outputs against integer multiplication and check full-memory equivalence and exact per-input instruction deltas. Five structural corruptions are rejected.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized registered commands pass locally in 4.723 and 4.594 seconds. These are individual verification durations, not benchmark speedup claims. Both return `PASS_WORDRAM_UNIT_TWIDDLES` with the same scientific transcript hash `1426ba9939e19827ff842d16524f0bd726fd412a550c8643cc8fc251adb0b332`.
- Metadata/pins, committed bytes/modes/source history, AST compilation, function-size inspection and whitespace checks pass. The official 13-file committed export passes integrity checking; normal and optimized replay are also run from its read-only Git-free copy with an empty PATH. Source-hash receipts are generated on stdout; none is handwritten.

From the repository root with CPython 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/wordram-unit-twiddles/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/wordram-unit-twiddles/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/wordram-unit-twiddles
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/wordram-unit-twiddles --check-source-history
```

Another CPython 3.12 path may replace the local executable. All six external inputs are pinned at canonical main `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a` and declared for replay selection. No pending Git object or network is needed for the scientific replay.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

This preserves a cited bounded multiplier under its original residue/setup/initialization invariants. The structural transformer alone is not a verifier for arbitrary programs. The universal implication is the written scoped proof; the finite template census is not an all-operand or complete asymmetric-length census. No unrestricted instruction optimum, asymptotic saving or new kappa is claimed.

The selected recursive invoice differs from this exact ISA invoice. A selected consumer, conversions, physical costs and complete supplier admission remain open. No independent human or proof-kernel review, complete machine formalization, selected cold replay, Lean, Docker or approximate-backend replay is claimed. No local mathematical check is left solely to CI.

## Open next questions

- Prove and price one complete-state macro for a known nonunit twiddle. No other arithmetic specialization is included in this first improvement.
- Bind the refined kernel to one actual selected consumer and charge conversions, sizes, restoration and its machine model before making an exponent claim.

## Related open work

- [#6435](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6435) preserves the original bounded kernel’s assertion checklist under optimized Python. It changes verifier portability; this PR changes the literal arithmetic program and its ISA instruction count. That checklist is not replayed here, and its follow-up questions are not targets of this PR.

The live targeted Word RAM search also returned #956, which studies a different exact scalar/index RAM provider rather than this bounded NTT kernel. The merged #5886 address allocation is separate context, not an extended source question. Latest open PRs and local claims were refreshed before committing; canonical main remained unchanged. Completion refresh inspected this account's 9 other open PRs created since the advance CLAIM: #6795, #6796, #6797, #6798, #6799, #6800, #6801, #6803, #6804. They study different objects or contracts; none studies this bounded NTT arithmetic rewrite or computes its instruction counts. No additional predecessor computation was run.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks, `plan` and `replay (research/wordram-unit-twiddles)`, passed at exact head `b792a58669a3bd2372a38db567ba04241b562519` in [run 42229198584](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42229198584). The checks were read once after completion. Hosted replay runs the registered normal and optimized commands. Local normal/optimized checks, committed-byte/source-history checks and read-only Git-free export replays also passed. CI certifies the registered finite replay and source bindings, not independent human acceptance or a complete machine theorem. No failed or waived check remains.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** research

One isolated opt-in package. No shared code, frozen source, selected certificate or existing contributor credit is modified.
